content: {"rules": ["Model forecasts consistently overestimate prices, showing upward bias with lagging reaction to true market movements.", "Sentiment history rarely influences forecasts, suggesting sentiment has minimal predictive power in this context.", "True outcomes often exhibit mean-reversion after sharp spikes, particularly in the 70–73 range.", "Forecasts tend to overshoot true values in the early part of the 30-day window, especially when prices are rising.", "Model accuracy improves when true outcomes are near historical averages, indicating a calibration effect with price stability.", "Forecasting models show diminishing predictive power as prices approach or fall below 65, suggesting a structural market shift.", "Sentiment spikes (even at 0.33) do not significantly alter forecast trajectories, indicating sentiment is not a strong driver.", "True outcomes frequently deviate from forecasts in the final 5–10 days, suggesting model calibration issues or market volatility."]}
